en: Those twelve specific factors taught by the Sage as having arisen dependently—
They are correctly subsumed within the three categories of afflictions, karma, and suffering.
The first, eighth, and ninth [links] are afflictions; the second and tenth are karma;
and the remaining seven are suffering. Thus, these twelve factors are subsumed within the three categories. (Pshk 2)
From the three arises the dyad; from the dyad arise the seven;
from the seven, the three arise again; thus indeed the wheel of existence revolves.
Indeed, the entire world consists of cause and effect; there is no other sentient being here at all.
From empty phenomena alone do empty phenomena arise.

The reconnection of the aggregates and the absence of transmigration are to be understood by the wise through the analogies of recitation, a lamp, a seal, a mirror, a sound, a sun-gem, a seed, and sour gruel. Pshk 5.
He who imagines annihilation even regarding an extremely subtle entity does not perceive the meaning of dependent origination, for he lacks understanding.
Nothing is to be removed from this, nor is anything at all to be added;
reality is to be seen as it truly is, for one who sees reality is liberated.
The *Pratītyasamutpādahṛdayakārikā* composed by the master Nāgārjuna is completed.
